{{short description|Brazilian physicist (1920–2011)}}
[[File:Jaime Tiomno, sem data.tif|thumb|200px|Jayme Tiomno]]
'''Jayme Tiomno''' (April 16, 1920 in [[Rio de Janeiro]] &ndash; January 12, 2011 in Rio de Janeiro) was a Brazilian experimental and theoretical [[physicist]] with interests in [[particle physics]] and [[general relativity]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://agencia.fapesp.br/13315|title=Jayme Tiomno morre aos 90 anos|date=2011-01-13|publisher=[[Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo|FAPESP]]|language=Portuguese|accessdate=31 August 2012}}</ref> He was member of the [[Brazilian Academy of Sciences]] and a recipient of the [[Brazilian Order of Scientific Merit]]. He was the son of Jewish [[Russia]]n immigrants.

He was  a  founder  of the CBPF - [[Centro Brasileiro de Pesquisas Físicas]] (Brazilian Center of Physics Research) and  one responsible for the creation of the [[Brazilian Physical Society]]. In 1965, invited by [[Darcy Ribeiro]], he became professor at the [[University of Brasília]], but was later mandatorily retired by the [[Military dictatorship in Brazil|military regime]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=FAPESP |title=Jayme Tiomno morre aos 90 anos |url=https://agencia.fapesp.br/jayme-tiomno-morre-aos-90-anos/13315 |access-date=2026-08-10 |website=AGÊNCIA FAPESP |language=pt-BR}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Clemente |first=José Eduardo Ferraz |date=2005-12-19 |title=Ciência e política durante a ditadura militar: o caso da comunidade brasileira de físicos (1964-1979 |url=https://rbhciencia.emnuvens.com.br/rsbhc/article/view/587 |journal=Revista da Sociedade Brasileira de História da Ciência |language=pt |volume=3 |issue=2 |pages=198–198 |issn=0103-7188}}</ref>
